extracted.intended_audience: faculty members (Texas Southern University) and university researchers preparing grant proposals
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for faculty preparing research grant proposals for public and private funding sources, including a skeletal technical proposal outline, narrative and budget preparation, institutional review procedures, and compliance/reporting requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical proposal elements (required sections)
rubrics_metrics.description: Skeletal outline of elements normally required in proposal preparation: an abstract, a summary of facilities available, the budget necessary to carry out the desired research project, a list of faculty personnel and their qualifications, and a narrative account of relevant research, purposes and objectives of the proposed study, description of procedures, and the usefulness of the proposed research findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Exhibit 1 as the recommended format. Although some funders require additional information, this outline represents general requirements. Put budget on a new page. Include appendices only for supportive materials (vitae, letters of support, instruments). Appended items may be added but should not carry the burden of the request for support—the main body must demonstrate the PI's capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarity and quality of writing (document must stand alone)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proposal document is a communication instrument which will be evaluated by agency staff and external reviewers; it must be well written and capable of standing on its own merits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research proposals may be rejected if not clearly written. Use direct language, present ideas in a straightforward manner, avoid slang and unnecessary jargon. Ask colleagues (not too close to the problem) to critically evaluate the proposal before submission so reviewers can understand the basic rationale and design.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract: single-page, concise, lay-understandable summary
rubrics_metrics.description: The Abstract occupies a single page, identifies the proposal, and summarizes the contents concisely; it should be written in language understandable by an informed layman.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abstract should give a clear, concise, and complete view of the research effort, communicate the rationale for the project, and summarize activities, expected findings/implementation, and budget highlights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Problem statement and objectives (rationale)
rubrics_metrics.description: The first part tells why the research or related activity should be undertaken: includes a statement of the problem or purposes, review of literature and related research, concise statement of objectives, and any information necessary to establish a sound rationale.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide enough background and related research to justify the study and identify new dimensions or gaps addressed. Objectives should be concise and clearly connected to the problem statement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Description of activities/procedures (what/when/how/evaluation)
rubrics_metrics.description: This section tells what is to be done, when, and how; it delineates procedures, outlines program arrangements, describes materials to be produced, and explains how evaluation will be accomplished.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe experimental treatments, characteristics of samples, selection procedures, activities and outcomes, and how the evaluation will determine effectiveness. The description is the basis for determining the degree to which objectives can be accomplished.

rubrics_metrics.name: Implementation and use of findings (dissemination and impact)
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe how the results may be disseminated and/or implemented, what contribution to education and other fields can be expected, and what steps should be followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain anticipated uses of findings, target audiences, and concrete dissemination or implementation plans so reviewers can assess practical benefit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget: detailed, reasonable, and justified
rubrics_metrics.description: The budget should show reasonable estimates, be detailed enough to show careful analysis, and include justification for items.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List personnel by name, position, title, experience, responsibilities, and percent time committed. Identify consultants and show rates/days; note some agencies disfavor excessive use of consultants. Include sources and amounts of non-federal support and any conditions. Start budget on a new page and include indirect cost clarifications with Contract Officer if needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel and consultant identification and commitment
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel are a major determinant of capability; list key personnel and consultants with qualifications and level of commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain commitments from local faculty and staff for required time; show assurances (signed or documented) for percent time. For consultants, describe the type of consultative assistance required and show rate and days in personnel/budget. Avoid over-reliance on consultants unless technically necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities description and assurances of availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Describe facilities to be used and indicate the extent to which their use has been assured.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make arrangements for required space, secretarial assistance, student assistants, classrooms, housing (for institutes), and document commitments from department heads or administrators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appendices usage policy
rubrics_metrics.description: Appended items (vitae, letters of support, instruments) may be submitted as supportive information but should not carry the burden of the request for support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Main body must demonstrate the PI's capability. Use appendices for supplementary material only and adhere to page limits specified by funder; include instruments, interview guides, and vitae as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conformance to agency instructions, deadlines, and format
rubrics_metrics.description: Follow specific instructions provided in guidelines for each funding source regarding deadlines, number of copies, and format requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use checklists to ensure institutional procedures and agency guidelines are honored, format suggestions followed, and unusual or experimental procedures clarified. Include required forms and complete all agency-specified items.

rubrics_metrics.name: General evaluation criteria: significance/relevance and contribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposals are evaluated for their potential contribution to educational improvements and alignment with agency priorities; widely used criteria include significance and relevance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize the significance of the problem, expected contribution, and relevance to funder priorities. Address other specific evaluation criteria as appropriate to the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with special conditions (human subjects, IP, data)
rubrics_metrics.description: Special conditions may involve release of materials, data collection instruments, use of human subjects, clearance, patent and copyright policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Carefully read funder-specific requirements before submitting. Ensure human subjects protections and clearances are arranged, and specify copyright/patent handling plans if applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting, fiscal accountability, and recordkeeping
rubrics_metrics.description: Grant recipients must submit final technical reports and periodic fiscal reports as specified in the contract; accounting records are subject to inspection and audit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain duplicate records, keep receipts, requisitions and related materials accessible, establish rapport with campus fiscal/grants offices, and be prepared for audits by state and federal agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence of local commitment (matching or local support)
rubrics_metrics.description: Local contributions to cost, while not necessarily a measure of project's soundness, are considered evidence of local interest and commitment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an outline of sources and amounts of non-federal support and state any contingencies tied to that support. Demonstrating local buy-in strengthens proposals.
